cues.text: Hi, Mark. Hi, Gina. What can I help you with?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: So we were hoping you could help us with this extracurricular project.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Sure - what is the topic?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Attending business school.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: This sounds like a great idea. So you’re going to explain the requirements for getting into business school?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Not exactly. It will be more broadly about the experience - the academics, accommodation, and social experience that comes with being a part of business school.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: I see. So would your audience be the general public?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, we would probably want more to focus on members of the institution - we would especially like to reach individual applicants to the business school.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: I see. Now what form will this information be? You could give a talk to all the summer courses - all you would need is permission from the course director. Or you could pass out information outside the student union.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Those are both good ideas. What about sending out pamphlets in the mail?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Most college students never check their mail. Maybe you could make a video and show it on campus?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s a great idea. We’ll do the video
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: Great. And as members of the business school, do you have an incentive to attract new students? If so, this idea is a great way to do that.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: No, the idea actually came about because of how much students like us worry about their studies.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Yeah - when I got into business school, there were a lot of things I had not prepared for, so the video would cover a lot of things Mark and I wish we had known upon entering business school.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: What would you talk about first?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: The first and probably most important section would be academics.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Good idea. So would you provide guidance on what courses to take?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: We want to focus especially on the approaches professors take - their teaching methods. It is far different than what students are used to in high school, and even in liberal arts college.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: Good idea. And how long do you think you would spend explaining academics?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: We’ll probably spend 7 minutes on it
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: We also have some ideas for talking about housing, food options, and stuff like that. We’re not really sure how to tie it all together though.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: I think it would be suitable to title that section accommodation - what do you think?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That could work. We’ll definitely describe the different dining options at the cafeteria, and then walk students through flats and the grueling process of finding one near the business school campus.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Okay - so we would cover specifics on the cafeteria, as well as flats?
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: I think those are both helpful. We could spend about 6 minutes on accommodations, and be sure to touch on those specifically.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Great. Is there anything else you would talk about?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: We definitely want to go over the social aspect of attending school here
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: Of course. I think it’s good to have a little fun once in a while when you’re working so hard in school.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I think we are going to introduce new students to the disco that so many upperclassmen know and love. Maybe we’ll include a few other places too, but that’s the main one.
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: We’re also going to invite students to the international evening taking place in the first week of school as a great chance for our large international student population to meet a lot of other new students.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: It can definitely be hard to meet people as an international student. I think that is a great idea. You may want to spend slightly longer on this section than the other two.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Hm… how about 8 minutes?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: That sounds reasonable. So overall, the introduction should take 3 minutes, and then the conclusion should take 4, giving us a total of 28 minutes.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: I wouldn’t rush your introduction. Maybe give it between 4 and 6 minutes. The conclusion, though, can be shorter since it’s just a quick refresher of each of the topics. Give that not more than 2 minutes.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Okay. So in total the video should take about the same time, just more into and less conclusion?
cues.speaker: Mark

cues.text: Precisely.
cues.speaker: Gina

cues.text: Alright - we are going to get to work on our video. Thanks for your help!
cues.speaker: Gina
